source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 7 (Climate Change, Global Warming and Ozone Depletion).

sections.heading: 1. Greenhouse Effect and Global Warming
points: The **greenhouse effect** — greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat (infrared) and keep the Earth warm; natural and essential, but enhanced by human activity.
**Greenhouse gases (GHGs):** **carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), water vapour, CFCs, ozone**.
**Global warming** — the rise in Earth's average temperature due to increased GHGs (fossil fuels, deforestation).

sections.heading: 2. Effects of Climate Change
points: Melting glaciers and ice caps → **sea-level rise** (threatens coasts/islands).
More frequent **extreme weather** (heatwaves, floods, droughts, cyclones); shifting monsoon patterns.
**Ocean acidification, coral bleaching**, loss of biodiversity, threats to agriculture and water.
**Carbon footprint** = total GHGs emitted by an activity/person.

sections.heading: 3. Ozone Depletion
points: The **ozone layer** (stratosphere) absorbs harmful **UV radiation** (protects life; UV causes skin cancer, cataracts).
**Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS):** **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), halons** — release chlorine that destroys ozone.
The **'ozone hole'** over **Antarctica** was discovered (worst in the polar spring).
Ozone depletion is a **distinct problem** from global warming (though both are atmospheric).

sections.heading: 4. Global Responses
points: **Montreal Protocol (1987)** — to phase out ODS (very successful); the **Kigali Amendment (2016)** targets HFCs.
**UNFCCC (1992)** → **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** (binding targets for developed nations) → **Paris Agreement (2015)** (limit warming to well below 2°C, aim 1.5°C; nationally determined contributions).
**IPCC** — the UN body that assesses climate science.
India: **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** with 8 missions (e.g. National Solar Mission).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: GHGs: CO₂, methane, N₂O, water vapour, CFCs, ozone.
Ozone layer (stratosphere) blocks UV; ODS = CFCs, halons; ozone hole over Antarctica.
Montreal Protocol (1987) = ozone (ODS); Kigali Amendment (2016) = HFCs.
Climate: UNFCCC (1992) → Kyoto (1997) → Paris (2015, <2°C, aim 1.5°C).
IPCC = climate science body; India = NAPCC (8 missions).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Montreal Protocol (1987) = ozone (ODS)**; **Paris Agreement (2015) = climate/GHGs** (do not confuse).
The **ozone hole is over Antarctica**.
**Ozone depletion ≠ global warming** (distinct problems).
**Kyoto Protocol (1997)** set binding targets for **developed** countries; **Paris (2015)** uses voluntary NDCs.
